newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Officials expect little from Arafat-Levy meeting.
newsitem.headline: Officials expect little from Arafat-Levy meeting.

text.p: Another handshake and a photo opportunity are about all officials expect from Tuesday's meeting between the PLO's Yasser Arafat and Israel's David Levy.

The Palestinian President is scheduled for talks with Israel's foreign minister in Brussels as disputes between the two sides over settlements and security nudge their peacemaking crisis into its fifth month.

The meeting is the highest Israel-PLO contact since April and follows Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's decision to dispatch his senior adviser to Washington for peace consultations, but a formula for reviving talks remained elusive.

"I'll meet him (Arafat) and we have things to talk about," Levy told Israel's Channel Two on Monday, adding quickly: "But there isn't some sort of expectation for the sake of which I'm travelling all the way to Belgium."
Palestinian Authority member Hanan Ashrawi said the meeting was little more than an Arafat gesture to Europeans bent on carving out an EU role in Middle East peacemaking.
"I think it's simply a gesture from President Arafat to the Europeans," she told Reuters.

Palestinians demand a freeze in Israeli settlement building in the occupied West Bank and Gaza Strip as the price for bringing Arafat back to the bargaining table. Isreal rejects even a temporary halt.
Asked if Levy and Arafat could make substantive progress in Brussels at the 15-member European Union's foreign ministers' meeting, Ashrawi said: "I doubt it."

Israel's groundbreaking in March on a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem -- which Palestinians regard as the capital of their future state -- launched the deadlock and triggered a wave of Arab protests.
A 14-year-old Palestinian boy shot by Israeli soldiers in clashes in Hebron two weeks ago died of his wounds and was buried on Monday.
Israel views East Jerusalem, which it captured in the 1967 Middle East war and later annexed, as part of its unified capital.
"I think it's always unhealthy to have overblown expectations because then disappointment sets in," Netanyahu's communications chief, David Bar-Illan told Reuters.

Netanyahu again demanded on Monday that Arafat's Palestinian Authority investigate allegations that senior security officials sent three police officers, now in Israeli custody, to attack Jews in the West Bank.
A PLO official said a senior police officer at the centre of the case had been arrested by the Palestinians.
"We don't think anybody should receive a prize for their willingness to return to the negotiating table," Bar-Illan said.

In the West Bank, Palestinian police said they had uncovered ready-to-use explosives and disguises at an apartment near Bethlehem which they suspected was a bomb laboratory of the anti-Israeli Hamas movement.

Netanyahu has demanded that Palestinians do more to crack down on Moslem guerrilla groups opposed to Israeli-PLO peace accords. "I would want to see these efforts done continuously," the Israeli leader said.
